metadata.title: The Request, Not the Change.
metadata.subtitle: The Change Request Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when you ask Claude to create a 'change request', does it make the change, or write up the request for someone else to approve? Lands the carry-out that change-request is a request, not the change — it writes the impact, the risk, and the rollback plan for approval, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed change request means Claude makes the change. It doesn't — it writes up the request: the impact, the rollback plan. So: how do I get Claude to request a change to my system?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is change-request — a single SKILL.md file, about three kilobytes. It's the whole instruction set, written in plain language, with no hidden logic underneath it. Claude reads it, then acts on what it says. The file is the program.

Its job, word for word: create a change management request with impact analysis and rollback plan. It triggers on requests like proposing a system or process change that needs approval, preparing a change record for CAB review, documenting risk and rollback steps before a deployment, or planning stakeholder communications for a rollout. Once triggered, Claude reads the Steps section and runs them in order — linear, no branching unless a step says so.

production_viz.label: HOW IT GETS PICKED UP
production_viz.caption: only runs when the words match

beats.narration_text: That's a request, not the change. The skill writes up the proposal — the impact, the risk, the rollback plan — for someone else to approve. Run it on the same proposed change twice, and the request comes back the same both times. But it only covers what you tell it — anything outside the described change is outside what this skill sees.

production_viz.label: A REQUEST, NOT THE CHANGE
production_viz.caption: it proposes the change, it doesn't execute it

beats.narration_text: change-request doesn't make the change — it writes the request: the impact, the risk, the rollback plan, for someone else to approve, the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to create a change management request for a system change — read the change-request skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That clause matters: having Claude explain itself first, before it acts, is how you actually see the instructions it's following, not just the result.
